title: Voyages of Wang Dayuan
summary: Wang Dayuan, a Chinese merchant-traveller from Quanzhou, made two sea voyages, probably 1330 to 1334 and 1337 to 1339, about eight years in all. Accounts place him in the Maldives in winter 1330 and in South India in spring 1331. His book Daoyi zhilue, completed in 1349, records over 220 foreign places, mostly in maritime Asia, and Zheng He later used it as a key travel guide.

uncertainty.note: Su Jiqing’s timeline calls the dates estimates: departure 1330, return 1334, second departure 1337, return 1339. His own text records winter 1330 at Dafoshan (Sri Lanka coast). The Asian Review of Books says the Maldives in winter 1330 and South India in spring 1331.

beats.caption: Wang Dayuan sails from Quanzhou, reaches the Maldives in winter 1330 and leaves for South India in spring 1331.
He is thought to return to China in 1334, and to leave again in 1337 on a second voyage that ends in 1339.
He completes Daoyi zhilue in 1349, covering over 220 foreign places; Zheng He later uses it as a key guide.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the two sources differ on stage detail (Su Jiqing has Dafoshan on the Sri Lanka coast in winter 1330; the review has the Maldives in winter 1330), so Dafoshan is not pinned and the Maldives and Quanzhou waypoints share the year 1330. Voyage dates are estimates per Su Jiqing. Other places named only in search snippets were not used. Return waypoint reuses the Quanzhou point.
